Subject: Follow-up + integration questions after demo

Thanks again for the demo this morning — good run-through. Per our notes, the eng team has a handful of specific items they want clarified before we lock in the POC scope. I captured them below. Could you confirm feasibility and rough effort? Also attaching the architecture sketch we discussed.

1) SDK + auth: we plan to integrate via your SDK (Node + Python). Do you recommend API keys or OAuth for server-to-server calls? We need short-lived creds and automatic rotation. Any boilerplate for token refresh?

2) Routing / model variants: we want predictable latency for chat-heavy flows but lower cost for bulk embedding jobs. Can requests be pinned to a region/model tag and fall back to a lower-cost variant automatically? How does routing interact with Dedicated pools?

3) Structured output / tool-calling: when we need deterministic JSON responses (e.g., extracts for our ingestion pipeline) should we use structured output enforcement or build a separate tool-calling step? Concerned about hallucinated fields.

4) Embeddings + reranking: best practice to compute embeddings in batches vs streaming? Any recommended dimensionality and how to handle incremental reindexing? Also, how do you suggest we combine semantic score + exact-match signals for rerank?

5) Request/response schema questions: chat vs completions differences for tokenization, max_tokens, stop behaviors, and streaming semantics — particularly: if we stream tokens, are stop tokens guaranteed to cut the stream cleanly? What about partial tokens during streaming and token accounting for billing?

6) Anything we should pre-provision (Dedicated) to meet 99th percentile latency targets for 1k qps during demo spikes?

Request: Can you reply with short answers and an action plan (owner + ETA) for the POC?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Li

Hi Sarah — great working session earlier. High level answers below; Dev will follow with a short technical note and code snippets. We attached our integration guide + a small SDK snippet for quick reference.

Quick answers (TL;DR):
- SDK + auth: recommend short-lived tokens via OAuth or mTLS for customer-hosted Private deployments; for Hosted/Dedicated, use API keys + optional short-lived session tokens. We have a token-refresh helper in the SDK. (Action: Dev to provide snippet)
- Routing/model variants: yes — routing policies support region pinning + model-fallback rules and Dedicated pools can be targeted with tags.
- Structured output vs tool-calling: prefer structured output enforcement for simple extraction; use tool-calling for side effects or when you need to guarantee external function invocation.
- Embeddings/rerank: batching is more efficient for large backfills; use incremental batch windows for reindex. Combine semantic cosine score with exact-match boost in the reranker stage.
- Chat vs completions: chat is stateful and manages system/user roles; completions are single prompt. Token accounting and max_tokens semantics are consistent, but stop tokens in streaming are advisory — we strip/truncate on the server if needed. Dev will expand.
- Provisioning for spikes: suggest a Dedicated burst pool with autoscale floor set to your 99th percentile target. We can run an SLO exercise in the POC.

Next steps:
- Dev (dev_patel) provides a technical note + SDK snippets by EOD 2026-10-12 (owner: dev_patel).
- We draft a one-page mutual action plan + cost estimate (owner: aditya_rao) by 2026-10-13.
- Schedule 30m deep-dive with your eng team for 2026-10-14.

Will loop in Marissa for SLAs and Dedicated pricing.

Best,

Subject: RE: Follow-up + integration questions after demo — technical note

Hi Sarah — following up with more granular details and concrete recommendations. I tried to keep this compact; happy to expand on any part in the 30m follow-up.

1) SDK + auth
- Hosted/Dedicated: we support API keys and session tokens. Recommended flow: create a short-lived session token (1h) using your API key via server-side exchange. The SDK exposes a refreshSession() helper that rotates tokens before expiry. This prevents long-lived keys being present on ephemeral hosts. Example pseudo:

  // pseudo-Node
  const session = await Redwood.auth.exchangeApiKeyForSession({ apiKey: process.env.RD_API_KEY });
  sdk.setToken(session.token);
  setInterval(async () => { if (session.expiresIn < 300) { session = await refreshSession(); sdk.setToken(session.token); } }, 60000);

- Private (VPC/on-prem): strongly recommend mutual TLS (mTLS) + short-lived certs issued by customer KMS. We provide Helm hooks for cert rotation.

2) Routing / model variants
- Policy engine supports rule sets: by region, by cost tier. You can tag requests with routeHint: {region: "us-west-2", tier: "low-cost"}. If the preferred model is unavailable, the engine will fall back to the next compatible variant (configurable order).
- Dedicated pools can be addressed with poolId or poolTag; autopromote/demote rules supported.

3) Structured output / tool-calling
- If your extractor schema is stable and you need strict field-level validation, use structured output (we run a post-generation schema validator and emit a validation score). This reduces downstream parsing but can still hallucinate unexpected values — we recommend a confidence threshold plus a lightweight ruleset to drop invalid fields.
- Use tool-calling when you need guaranteed invocation of an external op (e.g., enrichment webhook, DB write). Tool-calling is transactional on our side: we guarantee we attempted the call; you should implement idempotency keys.

4) Embeddings + reranking
- Batching: for initial bulk and reindexing, batch up to 1024 items per request (subject to sequence length). For real-time small writes, use single-item calls.
- Dimensionality: default 1536 is a good tradeoff; 768 works for smaller models and reduces storage.
- Re-ranking: convert embeddings -> candidate retrieval -> rerank stage where you combine scores. Example formula: final_score = alpha * semantic_cos + beta * exact_match_boost + gamma * recency_score. We recommend cross-encoder reranker for top-10 candidates if latency budget allows.

5) Chat vs completions (tokenization, max_tokens, stop, streaming)
- Tokenization: both endpoints use the same tokenizer backend; however, chat has an internal chat-history prefixing strategy which affects token counts. When computing max_tokens usable for user reply, subtract the history tokens. SDK helpers can estimate token usage client-side.
- max_tokens: server enforces the cap; if you request a completion that would exceed max_tokens, we truncate the output to fit. For chat, the system may truncate older messages to respect context window (configurable).
- stop tokens: stop sequences are advisory during streaming. The streaming layer attempts to stop at the first completed stop pattern, but partial token boundaries can make an exact cut ambiguous. We post-process the final message on the server to ensure stop semantics are honored before returning the final archived result. For strict enforcement in downstream pipelines, request short tokens and run a final regex validation step on the archived response.
- streaming semantics: we stream delta tokens (utf-8 chunks); billing counts tokens as soon as they are generated server-side. There can be a small window where a streamed token is emitted then truncated by stop logic; you will be billed for generated tokens, not for truncated archival length.

6) Provisioning for spikes
- For 1k qps chat spikes: reserve a Dedicated pool sized for baseline qps and enable burst autoscale to GPUs of the next higher tier. Set cold-start buffer zero for demos to avoid queuing. We can run a perf sim with your sample traces to produce an SLA target and cost estimate.

Code snippets and config (attached sdk-snippet.txt) show example routeHint usage and session refresh.
